page: Microsoft Azure E32pds_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by an Ampere ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processor operating at 3.0 GHz. Built on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, this instance provides 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs configured with a single thread per core, avoiding hyper-threading contention. The hardware architecture supplies 208 GB of system memory, yielding 6.5 GB of RAM per vCPU, alongside 1288 GB of local SSD temporary storage. Discrete graphics processing units are not present in this configuration.

Benchmark testing reveals stable multi-threaded execution and balanced memory throughput across varied workloads. While single-core Geekbench metrics show modest throughput at 1122.0 points, the instance demonstrates multi-core scalability with a Geekbench multi-core score of 13049.0 and a multi-core stress-ng result of 57247.25. Uncached large-block memory read bandwidth reaches 170.75 GB/sec, supporting high-throughput data operations such as 41.96 million Redis SET operations per second. However, compute tasks requiring advanced vector extensions or large language model inference show constrained output due to architecture limitations.

The 1:1 physical core allocation offers predictable latency and cost-efficient core density compared to traditional x86 alternatives, though workloads must be compiled for ARM64 architectures. The system is well configured for memory-intensive applications that utilize local high-speed scratch disk, such as in-memory data structures, distributed NoSQL and relational databases, parallelized code compilation, and ETL data staging.
description: Microsoft Azure E32pds_v5 is an ARM64 memory-optimized virtual machine powered by a 32-core Ampere ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processor clocked at 3.0 GHz. The instance delivers 32 dedicated vCPUs with a 1:1 physical core ratio, 208 GB of system memory (6.5 GB per vCPU), and 1288 GB of integrated local SSD storage, without GPU acceleration. Benchmark evaluations show balanced multi-threaded performance and strong memory throughput, achieving 41.96 million Redis SET operations per second, despite moderate single-threaded execution rates. The dedicated single-thread-per-core topology ensures consistent performance without noisy-neighbor thread contention. This hardware balance makes the E32pds_v5 suitable for memory-intensive enterprise tasks, such as distributed database clusters, caching tiers, parallel compilation pipelines, and data processing workloads compiled for ARM64 platforms.
